extracted.intended_audience: employees, peers, managers, and HR practitioners writing or implementing workplace peer/360-degree reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing constructive, ethical, and actionable peer performance reviews (360 feedback) that balance recognition and improvement. Includes structure, examples, anti-patterns, and recommended frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: identify areas for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review feedback can illuminate blind spots in employees’ self-assessments or self-understanding and can reinforce manager feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer feedback to highlight concrete areas where the employee can improve; tie critiques to observable behavior and past examples so the recipient understands what to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: acknowledge strengths and provide recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviews are an opportunity for employees to receive recognition from a sampling of their professional community, not just direct managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out specific strengths and how they contribute to team success; recognition supports engagement and retention. Give concrete examples of impact (e.g., saved $25M by creating a workaround).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare by tracking notes and examples year-round
rubrics_metrics.description: Take notes throughout the year for peer reviews so you’re not starting from scratch during review cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track feedback in a performance management system or private folder with project notes, examples of collaboration, patterns in performance, and dates of incidents to make feedback accurate and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure feedback into Strengths / Areas for improvement / Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to provide feedback that touches on the following sections: Strengths, Areas for improvement, Opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a downloadable template or create a consistent formal structure; this helps recipients compartmentalize feedback. Within sections, go from broad impressions to specific examples and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear formatting: headings, subheadings, and readable organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Within your three categories, consider using headings and subheadings to improve readability and help employees better digest peer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, well-formatted peer review makes it easy for colleagues to read, understand, internalize, and act on feedback. Prefer concise paragraphs and bullet points for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus constructive criticism on skills/behavior, not personal attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuable constructive criticism focuses on how people can improve specific areas of their performance rather than on personal shortcomings. Personal attacks should be avoided entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame problems as skills or knowledge that require focus or action (so the message elicits change). Avoid labeling the person (e.g., 'is disorganized'); instead describe observable behaviors and their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific: provide examples and link actions to impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing specific examples and linking actions to their impact is most effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe discrete events (what happened), the behavior observed, and the tangible outcome (impact). Include dates, context, and consequences where relevant to make feedback actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praise should be specific, concise, and evidence-backed
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition and praise can (and should) take many forms; share praise that is specific, concise, and backed up by real-life examples and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of vague compliments, cite concrete contributions (mentoring that led to promotions, initiative that filled a skill gap) and summarize the effect on team or company outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established frameworks (SBI, SWOT) to structure feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a professional framework, like Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI)™, ensures you can tie feedback to discrete events and describe the impact. SWOT can also dissect strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply SBI to describe situation, specific behavior, and resulting impact. Use SWOT to contextualize development opportunities and strengths relative to external factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be objective: focus on observable facts not opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback needs to focus on observable facts rather than personal opinions or impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace vague judgments ('You need to be a better communicator') with concrete observations ('I noticed gaps in how idea 1, 2, 3 were communicated in our meeting') and provide recommendations or training opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame misses as opportunities with actionable recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: When that ‘thing’ that didn't go well in the past is positioned as a skill or knowledge that requires focus or action, it's often easier for the employee to ‘hear’ the message and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer clear next steps (e.g., schedule monthly one-on-ones, change Slack notifications, request a second set of eyes) and tie them to intended outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague or fluffy praise and replace with specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid generic statements like 'a great co-worker' that provide little actionable insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show what makes the person 'a great co-worker' by describing behaviors (mentoring, positive attitude) and measurable results (promotions, filled skill gaps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations: avoid bias, personal criticisms, and malice
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviews should focus on professional performance and project outcomes, not personal criticisms or attacks. Anonymous reviews can encourage candor but raise concerns about bad actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do a final read-through for bias or personal attacks. Base critiques on corroborated observations and avoid intentionally barbed or mean-spirited comments; aim to support colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalize with a read-through and use templates/checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Do a final read-through to ensure no revisions are needed and that your comments are clear, concise, and free of personal attacks or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review templates or checklists to ensure you've covered strengths, opportunities for improvement, and praise. Ensure clarity, conciseness, and actionable guidance before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design feedback to support continuous improvement and self-awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective feedback can catalyze self-awareness and understanding needed to make professional changes; repeated themes across reviewers are particularly powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for feedback that helps the recipient see patterns, prioritize development, and take concrete next steps; frame feedback to encourage learning rather than punishment.
